Angel. What pity that we cannot incorporate these creations of Fancy; the very thought of them thrills

 Her voice . . . calm of thought] ‘His mind . . . thirsts for intercourse with an intelligence similar to
itself. He images to himself the Being whom he loves’ (S.’s Preface). Cp. ‘On Love’ (Prose 169–71) and
L&C II xxxi 4–6: ‘Hers too were all my thoughts, ere yet, endowed/With music and with light, their
fountains flowed/In poesy’. The impulse is equalitarian, not narcissistic: cp. Erasmus: ‘It is an especyall
swetnes to have one with whom ye may communycate the secrete affectyons of your mynde, with whom
ye may speake even as it were with your owne selfe’ (In Laude and Prayse of Matrymony Sigs. Cvi–Cviv).
